tools.name: security.authenticate
tools.description: Authenticate this MCP session. Required before any other security-mcp tool can be used when SECURITY_MCP_SHARED_SECRET is set on the server. Pass the exact value of that environment variable as `token`. After three failed attempts the server process will exit.

token.description: The value of SECURITY_MCP_SHARED_SECRET configured on the security-mcp server.

tools.name: security.logout
tools.description: Explicitly invalidate the current MCP session. After calling this, all security-mcp tools will require re-authentication via security.authenticate. Satisfies OWASP ASVS V3.3.1 (session invalidated on logout).

tools.name: security.start_review
tools.description: Start a stateful security review run, lock the scan mode, and return a run ID for ordered execution and attestation. OPERATING MANDATE: 90% fixing, 10% advisory. You do not list vulnerabilities and walk away — you write the fix, implement the control, and enforce the policy. Defaults to auto-apply; pass remediationMode: 'detection_only' for a report-only run. For a one-shot 'fortify'/'lock down X' request, call security.fortify instead — it auto-applies, resolves scope from natural language, and selects the specialist team.

mode.description: Required scan scope mode for this review.

remediationMode.description: Optional. Defaults to 'auto_apply' — fixes findings automatically as they are discovered, implements the control, and re-runs the gate until PASS. Set to 'detection_only' to report findings without modifying any files.

targets.description: Required for folder_by_folder and file_by_file modes. Relative folders/files to evaluate.

baseRef.description: Only for recent_changes mode. Base git ref, default origin/main.

headRef.description: Only for recent_changes mode. Head git ref, default HEAD.

tools.name: security.fortify
tools.description: One-shot: fortify / lock down / harden a named surface (forms, login, an API, the AWS account, or the whole codebase) to enterprise production grade in a single call. Always auto-applies — no remediationMode question, no confirmation gate. Resolves the target to concrete files via repo search and pre-selects the specialist agent team (a generic core app-security team for any named surface, plus cloud/crypto/AI/mobile/supply-chain specialists when those domains are signaled). Use this for plain 'fortify'/'lock down X'/'harden to production grade' requests instead of chaining start_review manually.

target.description: Free-text description of what to fortify, e.g. 'forms', 'the login flow', 'our API', 'the AWS account', 'the whole codebase'. Omit to fortify the entire codebase. This is the one-shot entry point: it starts an auto-apply review, resolves scope, and selects the specialist agent team for you — no remediationMode question, no confirmation gate.

mode.description: Optional scope override. When set, targets/baseRef/headRef are used verbatim and no natural-language scope resolution runs.

targets.description: Optional explicit folders/files, paired with mode.

stackContext.description: Optional detected tech stack, forwarded to the agent run (enables cloud/AI/mobile specialists for whole-codebase runs).

tools.name: security.attest_review
tools.description: Generate a security review attestation with integrity hash and optional HMAC signature.

signatureEnvVar.description: Optional env var containing a dedicated HMAC attestation key. Must be SECURITY_ATTEST_KEY or SECURITY_ATTEST_KEY_<SUFFIX>.

tools.name: security.run_pr_gate
tools.description: Run the security policy gate for recent changes, selected folders, or selected files. Returns PASS/FAIL plus findings and required actions.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

mode.description: Scan scope mode. recent_changes (default) uses git diff; folder_by_folder scans one or more folders; file_by_file scans explicit files.

targets.description: Required for folder_by_folder and file_by_file modes. Relative folders/files to evaluate.

baseRef.description: Base git ref for diff (e.g. origin/main). Optional.

headRef.description: Head git ref for diff (e.g. HEAD). Optional.

tools.name: repo.read_file
tools.description: Read a file from the repo workspace.

tools.name: repo.search
tools.description: Search the repo for a regex or string. Returns matches with file + line numbers.

isRegex.description: Treat query as regex. Default false.

tools.name: security.get_system_prompt
tools.description: Return the full security engineering system prompt. Optionally customized with your stack, cloud provider, and payment processor. Use this as the system prompt to configure Claude as an elite security engineer for your project. Core operating ratio: 90% fixing, 10% advisory — write the fix, implement the control, enforce the policy.

stack.description: Your tech stack, e.g. 'Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, AWS Lambda'. Appended as a Scope section to the prompt.

payment_processor.description: Payment processor in use, e.g. 'Stripe', 'Braintree', 'Adyen', or 'none'.

tools.name: security.threat_model
tools.description: Generate a STRIDE + PASTA + ATT&CK threat model template for a described feature or component. Returns a structured Markdown document ready to fill in.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

feature.description: One or two sentences describing the feature or component to threat-model. Example: 'OAuth 2.0 login flow with PKCE and session cookies'.

surfaces.description: Attack surfaces involved. Defaults to all.

tools.name: security.checklist
tools.description: Return the pre-release security checklist, optionally filtered by attack surface (web, api, mobile, ai, infra, payments, all).

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

surface.description: Filter checklist by attack surface. Default: all.

tools.name: security.generate_policy
tools.description: Generate a security-policy.json for your project based on your active surfaces and cloud provider. Save the output to .mcp/policies/security-policy.json.

surfaces.description: Active surfaces in your project. Determines which gate requirements are included.

cloud.description: Primary cloud provider. Adjusts cloud-specific evidence expectations.

tools.name: security.scan_strategy
tools.description: Create an exhaustive security scan plan and enforce a required user choice: folder_by_folder, file_by_file, or recent_changes.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

mode.description: Required scan mode. Ask the user to choose before starting review.

targets.description: Required for folder_by_folder and file_by_file. Relative folders/files to evaluate.

baseRef.description: Only for recent_changes mode. Base git ref, default origin/main.

headRef.description: Only for recent_changes mode. Head git ref, default HEAD.

tools.name: security.terraform_hardening_blueprint
tools.description: Generate an advanced Terraform hardening blueprint with secure module design, guardrails, and control mappings.

tools.name: security.generate_opa_rego
tools.description: Generate preventive OPA/Rego policy code for Terraform plans or CI pipelines. Requires explicit user consent first.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

policyPack.description: Policy pack to generate. Default: terraform_plan.

applySuggestion.description: Must be true before generating policy code. This forces explicit user consent.

tools.name: security.self_heal_loop
tools.description: Propose a human-approved self-healing improvement loop for this security setup. No adaptive change may be applied without explicit human approval.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

useCase.description: Short description of recurring security issues in this codebase.

findings.description: Recent recurring findings or control gaps.

approveAdaptiveUpdates.description: Must be true before suggesting any adaptive improvement. Human approval is mandatory.

tools.name: security.generate_compliance_report
tools.description: Map gate findings to a subset of a framework's controls (SOC 2, PCI DSS 4.0, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001). Marks each control satisfied / missing / unverified. This is a partial control mapping to aid evidence-gathering, NOT an audit or certification: a control is 'satisfied' only when a gate run completed its required workflow steps with no adverse finding, and 'unverified' whenever no gate run is supplied. GDPR and HIPAA are intentionally not offered.

runId.description: Optional security review run ID created by security.start_review.

framework.description: Compliance framework to map gate findings against. Partial control mappings only (SOC 2, PCI DSS 4.0, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001). GDPR and HIPAA are not offered: the control coverage for them was too thin to represent honestly.

persist.description: Write the report to .mcp/reports/ as a schema-versioned artifact with a SHA-256 digest. Default true: a report that leaves no file is not evidence.

tools.name: security.notify_webhooks
tools.description: Send security gate findings to configured external systems (Slack, Jira, PagerDuty, generic webhook). Configure endpoints via environment variables: SECURITY_SLACK_WEBHOOK, SECURITY_JIRA_URL+SECURITY_JIRA_TOKEN, SECURITY_PAGERDUTY_KEY, SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL.

runId.description: Security review run ID whose findings to send.

gateFailed.description: Whether the gate failed (determines alert severity).

tools.name: security.generate_remediations
tools.description: Maps each gate finding to a specific, actionable code-level remediation template. Called automatically after every gate FAIL. Returns ready-to-apply fix templates keyed by finding ID.

findings.description: Findings array from a gate run result.

tools.name: orchestration.create_agent_run
tools.description: Initialise a multi-agent orchestration run. Creates the agent-run directory and manifest. Call after security.start_review.

internetPermitted.description: Whether user permitted internet access for this run.

stackContext.description: Tech stack context derived from project scan.

agentNames.description: Optional pre-filtered specialist roster (security.fortify uses this for scoped runs). Omit for the full auto-selected roster.

tools.name: orchestration.update_agent_status
tools.description: Update an agent's lifecycle status (running/completed/completed_partial/failed). Called by each agent at start and end.

agentName.description: Name of the agent updating its status.

findingsPath.description: Workspace-relative path to the agent findings JSON file.

tools.name: orchestration.merge_agent_findings
tools.description: Merge and deduplicate findings from all agents. Sorts by severity (CRITICAL first). Hooks into the attestation flow via updateReviewStep. Call in Phase 3 after all agents complete.

runId.description: Review run ID — used to update the review step record.

tools.name: orchestration.executor_status
tools.description: Report which local LLM CLIs (claude / codex / copilot / ...) are installed and authenticated, what each can actually do, what is degraded, estimated wall-clock for a run, and whether a run could pass the capability gate. Costs zero model tokens. Call this BEFORE starting a run.

refresh.description: Re-probe binaries instead of using the 1-hour detection cache.

tools.name: orchestration.start_agent_run
tools.description: Execute the agent roster for real. Spawns a detached supervisor that drives every pending agent to a terminal state across all detected providers concurrently, surviving the end of this session. Returns in seconds with a pid and an estimate; poll orchestration.get_run_progress for status. Idempotent: re-running resumes a run whose supervisor died.

tools.name: orchestration.get_run_progress
tools.description: Progress for an agent run: phase, per-status counts, per-agent detail with execution provenance (provider, model, tier, transcript paths), and supervisor liveness.

tools.name: orchestration.cancel_agent_run
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running agent run. In-flight agents get 10s to stop and their records return to pending (not failed), so the run can be resumed later.

tools.name: orchestration.assert_run_complete
tools.description: Assert that every agent in a run reached a terminal state. THROWS while any agent is pending or running, so a partial run cannot be reported as finished. An evidenced completed_na counts as executed; pending does not. Pass dryRun:true to inspect without throwing.

dryRun.description: Return the status instead of throwing when incomplete.

tools.name: orchestration.ensure_skill
tools.description: Download a skill from the skills registry if it is not already installed or if it is outdated. Uses the skills-manifest.json registry. Requires internet access.

skillName.description: Name of the skill to ensure is installed (e.g. 'threat-modeler').

version.description: Required version; re-downloads if installed version differs.

tools.name: orchestration.read_agent_memory
tools.description: Read the persistent memory files for a named agent: patterns, false-positives, remediations, intel, and errors.

agentName.description: Agent name whose memory to read.

tools.name: orchestration.write_agent_memory
tools.description: Append new entries to an agent's persistent memory (patterns, false-positives, remediations, intel). Memory persists across runs and is used to calibrate findings.

agentName.description: Agent name whose memory to update.

addedBy.description: Only agents may add false-positive entries; blocks attacker-injected 'addedBy' fields

tools.name: orchestration.check_updates
tools.description: Check the npm registry and skills manifest for available updates to security-mcp and installed skills.

tools.name: orchestration.apply_updates
tools.description: Return update commands (choice: manual) or instructions for the agent to run them (choice: auto).

choice.description: auto = agent will run npm install command; manual = return commands for user to run.

tools.name: orchestration.verify_skill_coverage
tools.description: Verify that all 28 SKILL.md sections (24 numbered §1-§24 plus the 4 universal sections §EDGE-CASE-MATRIX/§TEMPORAL-THREATS/§DETECTION-GAP/§ZERO-MISS-MANDATE) have been covered by at least one agent in this run. Returns uncovered sections and a coverage percentage.

agentRunId.description: Agent run ID to verify coverage for.

tools.name: security.record_outcome
tools.description: Record the outcome of an agent resolving (or failing to resolve) a security finding. Feeds the pattern memory engine so the routing system learns which agents perform best on which finding types.

agentName.description: Name of the agent that worked on this finding.

resolved.description: True if the finding was successfully remediated.

falsePositive.description: True if this was a false positive. Default false.

remediationTemplate.description: One-line description of what was done to fix it.

durationMs.description: Time taken to resolve in milliseconds.

tools.name: security.get_routing
tools.description: Get the routing recommendation for a finding type. Returns which agent to route to, the success rate, and whether to escalate. Requires findingId in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

findingId.description: Finding ID to look up routing recommendation for.

tools.name: security.pattern_report
tools.description: Generate a full report of learned patterns and agent performance. Shows high-confidence routing decisions, low-confidence escalations, and top agents by finding type coverage.

tools.name: security.get_model_for_task
tools.description: Get the cheapest healthy model meeting the capability requirement for a given task type. Multi-provider: routes across Claude, GPT, Gemini, Cohere, and local Llama. Read-only/pattern tasks → cheapest light-tier model. Reasoning/remediation → cheapest standard-tier model. Respects per-provider circuit breakers (auto-failover on failure). Returns provider, model ID, cost, and rationale.

taskType.description: Task type to route. Max-power-by-default: security-critical reasoning tasks (remediation, threat_model, exploit_chain, ai_redteam, pentest, crypto_analysis, auth_analysis, code_review, etc.) route to the advanced tier automatically. Read-only/pattern tasks → cheapest light-tier model. Report generation → standard. Within a tier, routing picks the cheapest healthy provider meeting the floor. The budget safety valve may downgrade NON-protected advanced tasks to standard when spend crosses the threshold.

agentName.description: Optional agent name for usage tracking.

agentRunId.description: Optional agent run ID for correlating usage to a run.

tools.name: security.track_usage
tools.description: Record actual token usage after a model call completes. Updates running budget total and per-provider spend breakdown. Also resets the circuit breaker failure count for a successful provider call.

model.description: Model ID used (e.g. claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5, gpt-4o, gemini-1.5-pro).

tools.name: security.model_budget_status
tools.description: Return current model budget status: total spend, remaining budget, utilization percentage, per-tier call counts, per-task-type breakdown, and per-provider cost breakdown.

tools.name: security.get_provider_health
tools.description: Return circuit breaker health state for all LLM providers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Cohere, local). Shows consecutive failures, circuit open/closed status, and cooldown expiry. Use to diagnose why a provider is being skipped in smart routing.

tools.name: security.record_provider_failure
tools.description: Record a provider failure (connection error, auth error, rate limit). Increments consecutive failure count. Opens circuit breaker after 3 consecutive failures for 60 seconds. Call this when a model API call fails so the router skips that provider on next routing decision.

provider.description: Provider that failed. Increments consecutive failure count; opens circuit after 3 failures.

tools.name: security.reset_provider_circuit
tools.description: Manually close (reset) the circuit breaker for a provider. Use after confirming a provider is back online or to override an automatic failover during incident recovery.

provider.description: Provider whose circuit breaker to reset (close).

tools.name: security.init_chain
tools.description: Initialise the tamper-evident attestation chain for an agent run. Creates the genesis block. Must be called before attestAgent. Idempotent.

agentRunId.description: Agent run ID to initialise the attestation chain for.

tools.name: security.attest_agent
tools.description: Append a tamper-evident attestation for an agent's findings to the run chain. Links to the previous attestation via SHA-256 hash chain. Call after every agent completes.

agentRunId.description: Agent run ID this attestation belongs to.

agentName.description: Name of the agent completing its work.

findings.description: Agent findings to attest. Must match AgentFinding shape.

skillMdSectionsCovered.description: SKILL.md sections this agent covered. Attested via payloadHash.

capability.description: Capability record (model, tier, tools). Attested via payloadHash.

naEvidence.description: Evidence backing a completed_na verdict. Attested via payloadHash.

tools.name: security.verify_chain
tools.description: Verify the integrity of the attestation chain for an agent run. Recomputes all SHA-256 hashes and checks parent linkage. Returns valid: true only if every link is intact.

agentRunId.description: Agent run ID whose chain should be verified.

tools.name: security.get_chain
tools.description: Read the full attestation chain for an agent run for inspection. Returns all links with their hashes, finding counts, and timestamps.

agentRunId.description: Agent run ID to retrieve the attestation chain for.
